note: 84 AI-authored MCQs (batch A) covering the five digital-literacy competencies (dl_digital_foundations, dl_cyber_hygiene, dl_collaboration, dl_spreadsheets, dl_data_literacy), grounded in the real, publicly published content of the NIELIT Course on Computer Concepts (CCC) syllabus, CERT-In's Comprehensive Cyber Security Audit Policy Guidelines and Guidelines for Government Entities, I4C's Cyber Hygiene (Basic) Dos & Don'ts manual, and NITI Aayog's National Data and Analytics Platform Vision Document.

questions.locator: CCC syllabus, Unit 1.3.1 Components of Computer System
questions.source_excerpt: 1.3 Components of Computer System -- 1.3.1 Central Processing Unit
questions.question: In the NIELIT CCC syllabus's unit on computer basics, which component is described as the part of a computer system responsible for carrying out instructions and processing data?
questions.explanation: The CPU is the processing component of the syllabus's 'Components of Computer System' list. The VDU is an output device, the keyboard is an input device, and an external hard disk is a storage device -- none of them process instructions.

questions.source_excerpt: 1.3.2 Keyboard, mouse and VDU; 1.3.3 Other Input devices; 1.3.4 Other Output devices
questions.question: Under the CCC syllabus's 'Components of Computer System' topic, a mouse is grouped alongside the keyboard as which type of device?
questions.explanation: The syllabus groups keyboard and mouse together as input devices (1.3.2), with VDU/printer-type devices covered separately as output (1.3.4). Storage and processing are separate categories entirely.

questions.locator: CCC syllabus, Unit 1.4.2 Concept of Hardware and Software
questions.source_excerpt: 1.4.2 Software -- 1.4.2.1 Application Software; 1.4.2.2 Systems software
questions.question: The CCC syllabus splits software into two categories under 'Concept of Hardware and Software.' Which pair correctly names them?
questions.explanation: The syllabus's own sub-headings (1.4.2.1, 1.4.2.2) name application software and systems software as the two categories. The other pairings are real distinctions elsewhere in computing but are not this syllabus's stated split.

questions.source_excerpt: 1.4.3 Programming Languages
questions.question: Which of these topics is explicitly listed alongside hardware and software under Unit 1 ('Introduction to Computer') of the NIELIT CCC syllabus?
questions.explanation: Programming Languages (1.4.3) is the syllabus's own sub-topic under the hardware/software section. Cloud, machine learning, and blockchain are advanced topics not part of this foundational unit.

questions.source_excerpt: 1.7 Applications of IECT -- 1.7.1 e-governance; 1.7.2 Multimedia and Entertainment
questions.question: Under 'Applications of ICT' in the CCC syllabus, e-governance is grouped with which other application area?
questions.explanation: The syllabus names exactly two applications of ICT in this sub-section: e-governance and Multimedia and Entertainment. The other options are not part of this listed pair.

questions.source_excerpt: 1.5 Representation of Data/Information; 1.6 Concept of Data processing
questions.question: The CCC syllabus places 'Representation of Data/Information' immediately before 'Concept of Data Processing' in Unit 1. Why does this ordering make pedagogical sense for a foundational digital-literacy course?
options: Understanding how data is represented digitally is a prerequisite for understanding how a computer subsequently processes that data
Data processing must always be taught before data representation in any curriculum
The two topics are unrelated and the ordering is arbitrary
Data representation is only relevant to spreadsheet applications, so it must precede all other computing topics
questions.explanation: Learners need to grasp how information is encoded (e.g. as digital data) before they can meaningfully understand what 'processing' that data involves. The other options either reverse the logical dependency or dismiss a real pedagogical link.

questions.source_excerpt: 2.2 Basics of Operating System -- 2.2.1 Operating system
questions.question: In the CCC syllabus's operating-system unit, what is the operating system's basic role described as?
options: Managing the computer's hardware and software resources so applications can run
Only compiling programming language source code
questions.explanation: An operating system's foundational role, as introduced in this unit, is managing hardware/software resources -- internet connectivity, document formatting, and compiling are specific application-level tasks, not the OS's basic role.

questions.source_excerpt: 2.2.2 Basics of popular operating system (LINUX, WINDOWS)
questions.question: Which two operating systems does the NIELIT CCC syllabus name as examples under 'Basics of popular operating system'?
questions.explanation: The syllabus sub-topic explicitly names LINUX and WINDOWS as its two example operating systems; the other pairs are real operating systems but are not the ones named here.

questions.source_excerpt: 2.3 The User Interface -- 2.3.1 Task Bar; 2.3.2 Icons; 2.3.3 Start Menu; 2.3.4 Running an Application
questions.question: Per the CCC syllabus's 'User Interface' topic, which of these is listed as a component of a GUI-based operating system's interface?
questions.explanation: Task Bar is one of the four listed GUI-interface sub-topics (2.3.1-2.3.4). The other options are advanced, non-GUI technical tasks outside this foundational unit's scope.

questions.source_excerpt: 2.4 Operating System Simple Setting -- 2.4.1 Changing System Date And Time; 2.4.2 Changing Display Properties
questions.question: An officer needs to correct the system clock on a shared office computer after a power outage. Which CCC syllabus topic under 'Operating System Simple Setting' covers this task?
questions.explanation: Changing System Date and Time (2.4.1) directly matches correcting the clock. The other sub-topics cover display, printers, and mouse settings, none of which fix the clock.

questions.source_excerpt: 2.5 File and Directory Management; 2.6 Types of files
questions.question: The CCC syllabus's operating-system unit covers 'File and Directory Management' immediately followed by which related topic?
questions.explanation: Types of files (2.6) directly follows File and Directory Management (2.5) in the syllabus outline. Firewalls, database normalization, and cloud billing are unrelated, more advanced topics not part of this unit.

questions.source_excerpt: 5.2 Basics of Computer Networks -- 5.2.1 Local Area Network (LAN); 5.2.2 Wide Area Network (WAN)
questions.question: An organisation has offices in Delhi and Mumbai that need to exchange data over that long distance, while each office also has its own internal office network. Per the CCC syllabus's networking topic, how should the two needs be matched to LAN and WAN?
options: The internal office network in each city is a LAN, while the Delhi-Mumbai link connecting the two distant offices is a WAN
Both the internal office network and the Delhi-Mumbai link are LANs
Both the internal office network and the Delhi-Mumbai link are WANs
A WAN is used only within a single room, and a LAN spans entire cities
questions.explanation: The syllabus defines a LAN as covering a small, localized area (like one office) and a WAN as spanning much larger distances -- exactly matching the internal office network to LAN and the inter-city link to WAN. The other options invert or misapply these definitions.

questions.source_excerpt: 5.4 Services on Internet -- 5.4.1 World Wide Web and Websites; 5.4.2 Communication on Internet; 5.4.3 Internet Services
questions.question: The CCC syllabus separates 'World Wide Web and Websites' from 'Communication on Internet' as two distinct services on the internet. What best explains why they are treated separately?
options: Browsing websites and internet-based communication (e.g. email, messaging) serve different user needs, even though both rely on the same underlying internet infrastructure
Websites cannot be accessed using the same internet connection used for email
Communication on the internet does not require an internet connection
The World Wide Web is a different physical network from the internet
questions.explanation: The Web and internet communication are functionally distinct services (browsing vs. messaging) built on the same shared infrastructure, which is why the syllabus lists them as separate sub-topics. The other options describe technically false claims about connectivity or infrastructure.

questions.source_excerpt: 5.5 Preparing Computer for Internet Access -- 5.5.1 ISPs and examples (Broadband/Dialup/WiFi)
questions.question: A government office wants to connect its computers to the internet. Which CCC syllabus topic covers choosing between options like broadband, dialup, and WiFi?
questions.explanation: This sub-topic (5.5.1) explicitly names broadband, dialup, and WiFi as ISP connection examples. The other options belong to entirely different units (OS file management, spreadsheets, and collaboration).

questions.source_excerpt: 6.2 Web Browsing Software -- 6.2.1 Popular Web Browsing Software
questions.question: What kind of software does Unit 6 of the CCC syllabus ('WWW and Web Browser') primarily teach users to work with?
questions.explanation: Unit 6 is centred on web browsing software, as its own title and 6.2 sub-topic state. Spreadsheets and presentations are separate units, and email server administration is not covered at this foundational, user-facing level.

questions.source_excerpt: 6.4 Search Engines -- 6.4.1 Popular Search Engines/Search for content; 6.4.2 Accessing Web Browser; 6.4.3 Using Favorites Folder; 6.4.4 Downloading Web Pages; 6.4.5 Printing Web Pages
questions.question: An officer frequently revisits the same government scheme webpage while still connected to the internet. Which CCC syllabus sub-topic under 'Search Engines' covers saving that page for quick future access?
questions.explanation: Using Favorites Folder (6.4.3) is the bookmarking feature for quick return access while online. Downloading and printing save a local/paper copy rather than a quick browser shortcut, and 'Popular Search Engines' is about search, not revisiting a known page.

questions.source_excerpt: 6.4.4 Downloading Web Pages; 6.4.5 Printing Web Pages
questions.question: An officer needs to preserve an official circular published only as a webpage, for offline reference during a field visit with no internet access. Which CCC syllabus sub-topic is most directly relevant?
questions.explanation: Downloading Web Pages (6.4.4) saves a local copy usable without an internet connection. A Favorites/bookmark entry (6.4.3) still requires internet to reopen the live page, and search engines/browser configuration do not address offline access at all.

questions.source_excerpt: 7.2 Basics of E-mail -- 7.2.1 What is an Electronic Mail
questions.question: Per Unit 7 ('Communication and Collaboration') of the CCC syllabus, what foundational concept is introduced first under 'Basics of E-mail'?
questions.explanation: 'What is an Electronic Mail' (7.2.1) is the very first sub-topic under Basics of E-mail, before addressing, configuration, or spam handling are introduced.

questions.source_excerpt: 7.2.2 Email Addressing
questions.question: Which CCC syllabus sub-topic under 'Basics of E-mail' teaches the structure of an email address (e.g. username@domain)?
questions.explanation: Email Addressing (7.2.2) is the sub-topic on address structure. The other options cover client setup, organizing mail, and storing contacts -- different concerns.

questions.source_excerpt: 7.2.3 Configuring Email Client
questions.question: Before an officer can send or receive mail through a desktop email program, which CCC syllabus sub-topic must typically be completed first?
questions.explanation: Configuring the email client (7.2.3) -- setting up account details -- is the prerequisite step. Sorting, spam handling, and smileys are all activities that come after mail is already flowing.

questions.source_excerpt: 7.3 Using E-mails -- 7.3.1 Opening Email Client; 7.3.2 Mailbox: Inbox and Outbox
questions.question: In the CCC syllabus's 'Using E-mails' topic, the mailbox is described in terms of which two components?
questions.explanation: 7.3.2 names Inbox and Outbox as the mailbox's two components in this syllabus. The other pairings, while real email features generally, are not the pair named here.

questions.source_excerpt: 7.3.3 Creating and Sending a new E-mail
questions.question: An officer needs to send a fresh message (not a reply) to a colleague about an upcoming meeting. Which CCC syllabus sub-topic under 'Using E-mails' covers this action?
options: Creating and Sending a new E-mail
questions.explanation: Creating and Sending a new E-mail (7.3.3) is specifically about composing an original message, distinct from replying to or forwarding an existing one.

questions.source_excerpt: 7.3.4 Replying to an E-mail message; 7.3.5 Forwarding an E-mail message
questions.question: What is the key difference between 'Replying to an E-mail' and 'Forwarding an E-mail,' as distinguished in the CCC syllabus?
options: Replying sends a response back to the original sender, while forwarding sends the received message on to a new recipient
Replying and forwarding always go to the exact same set of recipients
Forwarding can only be done after the message has been printed
Replying deletes the original message while forwarding keeps it
questions.explanation: Reply routes a response back to the sender; forward routes the original message to someone new -- the core distinction the syllabus lists these as separate sub-topics for. The other statements misdescribe both actions.

questions.source_excerpt: 7.3.6 Sorting and Searching emails
questions.question: An officer's inbox has hundreds of messages, and they need to quickly locate all emails from a specific sender. Which CCC syllabus sub-topic addresses this need?
questions.explanation: Sorting and Searching emails (7.3.6) is exactly the skill for finding specific messages in a large inbox. The other sub-topics deal with unwanted mail, storing contacts, and catching typos, respectively.

questions.source_excerpt: 7.4 Advance email features -- 7.4.1 Sending document by E-mail
questions.question: Which CCC syllabus sub-topic under 'Advance email features' covers sharing a prepared document with a colleague via email?
questions.explanation: Sending document by E-mail (7.4.1) directly covers attaching and sharing files. The other options concern expressive symbols, behavioral norms, and basic client access.

questions.source_excerpt: 7.4.3 Using Address book
questions.question: Which CCC syllabus sub-topic covers storing colleagues' email addresses for quick reuse instead of retyping them each time?
questions.explanation: Using Address book (7.4.3) is specifically about saving contacts for reuse. The other sub-topics deal with locating messages, filtering unwanted mail, and messaging/etiquette respectively.

questions.source_excerpt: 7.4.5 Handling SPAM
questions.question: Why does the CCC syllabus include 'Handling SPAM' as part of collaborative, everyday email use rather than treating it purely as a technical security topic?
options: Because recognizing and appropriately managing unsolicited or unwanted mail is a practical, everyday skill for anyone collaborating over email, not just IT staff
Because SPAM only affects email servers and never reaches individual users
Because SPAM handling is identical to configuring a network firewall
Because the syllabus treats SPAM purely as a word-processing formatting issue
questions.explanation: Handling SPAM sits inside 'Advance email features' precisely because it is a routine user-level judgment call, not a server administration task -- which is why every officer, not just IT staff, needs this skill.

questions.source_excerpt: 7.4.2 Activating Spell checking
questions.question: Which CCC syllabus sub-topic helps an officer catch typing errors before sending a professional email?
questions.explanation: Activating Spell checking (7.4.2) is the sub-topic aimed at catching typos before sending. The other options concern emoticons, mailbox structure, and address format -- not error-checking.

questions.source_excerpt: 7.5 Instant Messaging and Collaboration -- 7.5.1 Using Smiley; 7.5.2 Internet etiquettes
questions.question: For workplace instant-messaging collaboration, the CCC syllabus pairs 'Using Smiley' with 'Internet etiquettes' in the same topic. What does this pairing suggest about responsible digital collaboration?
options: Both expressive elements (like emoticons) and behavioral norms (etiquette) shape how professionally a message is received, so both matter for collaboration
Smileys are a formal requirement in all official government communication
Internet etiquette only applies to email and never to instant messaging
Emoticons and etiquette are unrelated topics grouped together by coincidence
questions.explanation: Grouping tone-setting elements (emoticons) with behavioral norms (etiquette) under one heading reflects that both influence how a message lands in a workplace chat -- neither claim in the wrong options matches the syllabus's actual grouping or scope.

questions.source_excerpt: 7.5.2 Internet etiquettes
questions.question: An officer CCs an entire department distribution list on a message meant for only one colleague, triggering dozens of unnecessary 'reply-all' responses. Which CCC syllabus sub-topic on responsible teamwork is most relevant to preventing this?
questions.explanation: Internet etiquettes (7.5.2) covers responsible, considerate communication behavior, which includes avoiding unnecessary mass-CCs. The other sub-topics address contact storage, spelling, and account setup -- unrelated to this behavioral lapse.

questions.source_excerpt: 3.3 Opening and closing Documents -- 3.3.1 Opening Documents; 3.3.2 Save and Save as
questions.question: When a team is collaboratively revising a shared document, using 'Save As' rather than plain 'Save' is closest to which CCC syllabus concept?
options: Save and Save as -- creating a new version or copy of the document rather than overwriting the current file
questions.explanation: 'Save As' (part of 3.3.2) creates a distinct file/version, which is the basic mechanism behind keeping track of document revisions during teamwork. Print Preview, Table Manipulation, and Help are unrelated word-processing features.

questions.source_excerpt: 3.4 Text Creation and manipulation -- 3.4.4 Cut, Copy and Paste
questions.question: Two colleagues are combining sections they wrote separately into one shared report. Which CCC syllabus sub-topic under 'Text Creation and manipulation' covers moving text between documents?
questions.explanation: Cut, Copy and Paste (3.4.4) is the mechanism for moving text between documents. Changing case, borders/shading, and table drawing are formatting features unrelated to combining content.

questions.source_excerpt: 3.3.3 Page Setup; 3.3.4 Print Preview
questions.question: Before circulating a printed agenda for a meeting, which CCC syllabus sub-topics let an officer check how the document will look on paper?
questions.explanation: Page Setup (3.3.3) and Print Preview (3.3.4) are the syllabus's own sub-topics for checking a document's printed layout before circulating it. The other options are content-editing or formatting features, not print-readiness checks.

questions.source_excerpt: 8.3 Creation of Presentation -- 8.3.1 Creating a Presentation Using a Template
questions.question: An officer preparing slides for a departmental review meeting wants a consistent, ready-made design instead of building one from scratch. Which CCC syllabus sub-topic under 'Making small presentations' covers this?
options: Creating a Presentation Using a Template
questions.explanation: Creating a Presentation Using a Template (8.3.1) is specifically about starting from a ready-made design. The other sub-topics cover headers/footers, slide-show timing, and inserting objects -- later-stage tasks, not the initial design choice.

questions.source_excerpt: 8.7 Slide Show -- 8.7.1 Running a Slide Show; 8.7.2 Transition and Slide Timings; 8.7.3 Automating a Slide Show
questions.question: For an unattended kiosk display at a public information desk that should show scheme details on a repeating loop during an event, which CCC syllabus 'Slide Show' sub-topic is most directly useful?
questions.explanation: Automating a Slide Show (8.7.3) is built for exactly this unattended, looping-display scenario. Draw Table and Handling SPAM belong to entirely different units, and Using The Help is a general reference feature, not a presentation-automation tool.

questions.source_excerpt: 4. SPREAD SHEET -- 4.0 Introduction; 4.1 Objectives
questions.question: In the NIELIT CCC syllabus, spreadsheets are introduced as a tool primarily for what kind of work?
options: Organizing and computing structured, tabular data
questions.explanation: Unit 4 is dedicated to spreadsheets for structured, tabular data work. Prose documents, slide design, and email are the subjects of Units 3, 8, and 7 respectively.

questions.source_excerpt: 4.2 Elements of Electronic Spread Sheet -- 4.2.1 Opening of Spread Sheet
questions.question: Which CCC syllabus sub-topic under 'Elements of Electronic Spread Sheet' covers launching the spreadsheet application and starting a new worksheet?
questions.explanation: Opening of Spread Sheet (4.2.1) is the launch/start step. Addressing, printing, and saving are later steps in the same 4.2 sub-topic list, not the starting action.

questions.source_excerpt: 4.2.2 Addressing of Cells
questions.question: The CCC syllabus's spreadsheet unit covers 'Addressing of Cells.' What does cell addressing (e.g. A1, B2) let a user do?
options: Uniquely refer to a specific cell by its column letter and row number so formulas and functions can point to exact data
Change the font color of an entire worksheet at once
Convert a spreadsheet file into a presentation slide
Send the spreadsheet as an email attachment
questions.explanation: Cell addressing is the naming convention that lets formulas and functions reference exact data locations. The other options describe unrelated formatting, file-conversion, and emailing actions.

questions.source_excerpt: 4.2.4 Saving Workbooks
questions.question: After finishing a day's data entry, which CCC syllabus sub-topic under 'Elements of Electronic Spread Sheet' should an officer use to preserve their work for later?
questions.explanation: Saving Workbooks (4.2.4) is specifically about persisting the file. Addressing, printing, and opening are different actions in the same sub-topic list, not preservation of work.

questions.source_excerpt: 4.2.3 Printing of Spread Sheet
questions.question: An officer wants a hard copy of a completed data summary to attach to a physical file. Which CCC syllabus sub-topic covers this?
options: Creating Text, Number and Date Series
questions.explanation: Printing of Spread Sheet (4.2.3) directly covers producing a hard copy. The other sub-topics cover data-entry shortcuts, cell sizing, and calculation -- not printing.

questions.source_excerpt: 4.3 Manipulation of Cells -- 4.3.1 Entering Text, Numbers and Dates
questions.question: Which CCC syllabus sub-topic covers the basic act of typing text, numeric values, and dates into individual spreadsheet cells?
options: Creating Text, Number and Date Series
questions.explanation: Entering Text, Numbers and Dates (4.3.1) is the basic data-entry sub-topic, distinct from the automated series-filling, editing, and row/column-management sub-topics listed alongside it.

questions.source_excerpt: 4.3.2 Creating Text, Number and Date Series
questions.question: An officer needs a column pre-filled with consecutive dates (Day 1, Day 2, Day 3, and so on) without typing each one manually. Which CCC syllabus sub-topic covers this capability?
options: Creating Text, Number and Date Series
questions.explanation: Creating Text, Number and Date Series (4.3.2) is specifically about auto-filling sequences, unlike manual entry (4.3.1), cell sizing, or built-in functions.

questions.source_excerpt: 4.3.3 Editing Worksheet Data
questions.question: After entering data, an officer notices a figure was mistyped and needs to correct it in place. Which CCC syllabus sub-topic covers this?
questions.explanation: Editing Worksheet Data (4.3.3) covers correcting existing entries. The other sub-topics involve structural row/column changes, cell sizing, and printing, not correcting a mistyped value.

questions.source_excerpt: 4.3.4 Inserting and Deleting Rows, Column
questions.question: A new field office needs to be added as an extra row to an existing tabular dataset. Which CCC syllabus sub-topic covers this?
questions.explanation: Inserting and Deleting Rows, Column (4.3.4) is exactly the structural change needed to add a new row. Cell sizing, formulas, and charts do not add new rows.

questions.source_excerpt: 4.3.5 Changing Cell Height and Width
questions.question: Which CCC syllabus sub-topic covers adjusting a spreadsheet so that a long piece of text is not visually cut off within its cell?
questions.explanation: Changing Cell Height and Width (4.3.5) is the sizing adjustment sub-topic. Editing data, addressing cells, and saving workbooks do not affect how much of a cell's content is visible.

questions.source_excerpt: 4.4 Function and Charts -- 4.4.1 Using Formulas
questions.question: An officer wants a cell to automatically compute the total of two other cells whenever their values change. Which CCC syllabus sub-topic under 'Function and Charts' covers this?
questions.explanation: Using Formulas (4.4.1) is the sub-topic for writing an expression that recalculates automatically. Charts visualize data rather than compute it, Function covers named built-in operations (a related but separate sub-topic), and printing is unrelated.

questions.source_excerpt: 4.4.1 Using Formulas; 4.4.2 Function
questions.question: The CCC syllabus lists 'Using Formulas' and 'Function' as two separate sub-topics under 'Function and Charts.' What best distinguishes a spreadsheet formula from a built-in function?
options: A formula is any user-written expression combining cell references and operators, while a function is a predefined, named operation (e.g. a totalling or averaging routine) that can be used inside a formula
Formulas only work on text values, while functions only work on numeric values
Functions require an active internet connection to run, while formulas do not
There is no real difference; the two terms are always interchangeable in every spreadsheet package
questions.explanation: A formula is any expression the user constructs, while a function is a predefined named operation that can be embedded in a formula -- which is exactly why the syllabus treats them as related but distinct sub-topics. The other statements are factually wrong.

questions.source_excerpt: 4.4.2 Function
questions.question: An officer needs to quickly summarize a column of monthly expenditure figures into one total value, without manually adding each entry. Which CCC syllabus sub-topic best supports this?
questions.explanation: Function (4.4.2) covers built-in summarizing operations (such as totals), which directly matches this task. Addressing cells, drawing tables, and opening the spreadsheet do not perform calculations.

questions.source_excerpt: 4.4.3 Charts
questions.question: An officer wants to visually compare expenditure across five districts rather than reading a long list of numbers. Which CCC syllabus sub-topic under 'Function and Charts' covers this?
questions.explanation: Charts (4.4.3) is the visualization sub-topic for comparing values at a glance. Formulas and Function compute values but do not visualize them, and Saving Workbooks is unrelated to comparison.

questions.source_excerpt: 4.4.3 Charts
questions.question: For summarizing how a single budget total is divided among four departments, which visual best fits the CCC syllabus's 'Charts' sub-topic goal of clear visual summary?
options: A pie chart showing each department's share of the total
A spreadsheet cell with only the total typed in bold
A blank worksheet with no chart at all
questions.explanation: A pie chart is the standard way to show proportional shares of a whole, matching the 'part of a total' structure of the data. The other options provide no visual comparison at all.

questions.source_excerpt: 4.3.1 Entering Text, Numbers and Dates
questions.question: While entering data under the CCC syllabus's 'Entering Text, Numbers and Dates' sub-topic, an officer notices a date was typed inconsistently -- '01/02/26' in some rows and '1-Feb-2026' in others -- within the same column. Why does this matter for later spreadsheet work?
options: Inconsistent formats in the same column can prevent formulas, sorting, and functions from correctly recognizing the values as comparable dates
Spreadsheet software automatically standardizes all date formats regardless of how they are typed
Date format consistency only matters for printed output, not for calculations
It has no effect, since dates are always stored and treated as plain text
questions.explanation: Mixed date formats in one column risk being read as different data types, breaking sorting and date-based formulas -- exactly the kind of structured-data discipline the spreadsheets competency targets. The other options make false claims about automatic correction or irrelevance.

questions.locator: CCC syllabus, Unit 4 (Syllabus Outline table) and Unit 1 (for comparison)
questions.source_excerpt: Syllabus Outline: 1. Introduction to computer -- 2 theory, 1 tutorial, 4 practical; 4. Spreadsheets -- 4 theory, 2 tutorial, 10 practical
questions.question: Compared to Unit 1 ('Introduction to Computer,' 2 theory/1 tutorial/4 practical hours), how does the CCC syllabus's Unit 4 ('Spreadsheets,' 4 theory/2 tutorial/10 practical hours) emphasize learning?
options: It allocates more hours overall, with a strong emphasis on hands-on practical hours over theory
It allocates fewer total hours than Unit 1
It has zero practical hours, being purely theoretical
It has identical hour allocations to Unit 1
questions.explanation: Unit 4's 10 practical hours (versus Unit 1's 4) and higher totals overall reflect a hands-on, skill-building emphasis for spreadsheets. The other options misstate the actual hour allocations.

questions.locator: Comprehensive Cyber Security Audit Policy Guidelines, Section 5 Definitions (i)
questions.source_excerpt: Cyber Security Audit - A systematic and independent assessment of an organization's security controls, policies, and procedures to evaluate their effectiveness in protecting information systems and data from cyber threats.
questions.question: Per CERT-In's Comprehensive Cyber Security Audit Policy Guidelines, how is a 'Cyber Security Audit' defined?
options: A systematic and independent assessment of an organization's security controls, policies, and procedures
A one-time password reset performed after a data breach
A marketing review of an organization's IT vendor contracts
An informal, unscheduled chat between IT staff about security
questions.explanation: This is the guideline's own definition (Section 5). A password reset, a vendor-contract review, and an informal chat are not systematic, independent security assessments.

questions.locator: Comprehensive Cyber Security Audit Policy Guidelines, Section 3 Objective of the Document
questions.source_excerpt: Establish Uniform Standards: Ensure that all cyber security audits follow a common set of standards and procedures, thereby promoting consistency in audit quality, evaluation criteria, and reporting.
questions.question: One of the stated objectives of CERT-In's Audit Policy Guidelines is to 'Establish Uniform Standards.' What is this objective meant to achieve?
options: Consistency in audit quality, evaluation criteria, and reporting across different audits
Allowing each auditor to use entirely different, undocumented methods
Eliminating the need for any auditee cooperation
Replacing all audits with automated software scans only
questions.explanation: The guideline text explicitly links uniform standards to consistent audit quality, evaluation criteria, and reporting. The other options directly contradict the stated purpose of standardization.

questions.locator: Comprehensive Cyber Security Audit Policy Guidelines, Section 4 Applicability
questions.source_excerpt: This guideline...is applicable to...CERT-In empaneled Auditing Organizations...Auditee Organizations: It is the organization that owns or operates the systems...being evaluated
questions.question: CERT-In's Comprehensive Cyber Security Audit Policy Guidelines state that they apply to which two categories of entities?
options: CERT-In empanelled auditing organizations and auditee organizations
Only private banks, with no government bodies covered
Only individual citizens using personal devices
questions.explanation: Section 4 names exactly these two categories. Private banks alone, individual citizens, and foreign vendors are not how the guideline defines its applicability.

questions.locator: Comprehensive Cyber Security Audit Policy Guidelines, Section 5 Definitions (vii) Root Cause Analysis
questions.source_excerpt: Root Cause Analysis (RCA) - A systematic investigative process used to identify the fundamental causes or underlying factors that contribute to an incident, audit finding, or failure. RCA seeks to address the source of the issue rather than merely its symptoms
questions.question: Why does CERT-In's Audit Policy Guidelines' definition of Root Cause Analysis (RCA) emphasize addressing 'the source of the issue rather than merely its symptoms'?
options: Because fixing only the visible symptoms of an audit finding, without addressing its underlying cause, leaves the organization vulnerable to the same issue recurring
Because RCA is only meant to assign blame to individual employees
Because symptoms and root causes are always identical in cyber security incidents
Because RCA replaces the need for any corrective action
questions.explanation: Treating symptoms without fixing the underlying cause means the same finding is likely to reappear -- that is the practical reasoning behind the definition's emphasis. The other options misstate RCA's purpose.

questions.locator: CERT-In Guidelines for Government Entities, Section 3.1 Policy Measures
questions.source_excerpt: 3.1. Nominate a Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) for IT Security and provide the details of this CISO (Point of Contact) to CERT-In
questions.question: Per CERT-In's Guidelines for Government Entities, which role must senior management nominate for IT security and report to CERT-In as a point of contact?
questions.explanation: Section 3.1 explicitly requires nominating a CISO. A CFO, PRO, or cable installer are not the role this guideline requires as the security point of contact.

questions.locator: CERT-In Guidelines for Government Entities, Section 3.4 Policy Measures
questions.source_excerpt: Organisations should conduct an internal and external audit of the entire ICT infrastructure...Internal information security audit to be conducted at least once in 6 months. 3rd Party Security audits must be conducted at least once a year.
questions.question: According to CERT-In's Guidelines for Government Entities, how frequently must internal information security audits be conducted, at minimum?
options: Only once, when the system is first installed
Only after a confirmed breach has already occurred
questions.explanation: Section 3.4 states internal audits must occur at least once every 6 months. A one-time installation check, a 5-year cycle, or a purely reactive post-breach check do not meet this standard.

questions.locator: CERT-In Guidelines for Government Entities, Section 3.4 Policy Measures
questions.source_excerpt: 3rd Party Security audits must be conducted at least once a year. Services of CERT-In empanelled auditors may be utilized for the purpose of external audits.
questions.question: A government entity has just completed its internal 6-monthly ICT security audit. Per CERT-In's Guidelines, what additional external audit obligation still applies at least annually?
options: A third-party security audit, which may use CERT-In empanelled auditors
No further audits are required once the internal audit is done
A financial audit of the IT department's budget only
A customer satisfaction survey of citizens using e-governance services
questions.explanation: The internal audit does not replace the separate, at-least-annual third-party security audit requirement. A budget audit or satisfaction survey is not what this section requires.

questions.locator: CERT-In Guidelines for Government Entities, Section 4.1.2-4.1.3 Network and infrastructure security
questions.source_excerpt: Network should be properly segmented, with separate VLANs...Communication between different VLANs should be denied by default...The firewall rule set should deny traffic by default and a whitelist should be applied
questions.question: CERT-In's Guidelines for Government Entities describe both VLAN segmentation and firewall rules as following a 'deny by default' approach. What security principle does this reflect?
options: Only explicitly authorized traffic or connections should be allowed; everything else is blocked unless specifically permitted
All traffic should be allowed by default to maximize convenience for users
Firewalls and VLANs should never be deployed together in the same network
Denying by default means the network has no internet access at all
questions.explanation: 'Deny by default, allow by exception' is the least-privilege style principle described in both the VLAN and firewall passages. The other options describe the opposite approach or misread the guidance entirely.

questions.locator: CERT-In Guidelines for Government Entities, Section 3.3 Policy Measures
questions.source_excerpt: CISO should have a dedicated cybersecurity team, separate from IT operations and infrastructure team. The team would be responsible for: i. monitoring network's security...ii. conducting incident response iii. formulating, enforcing and reviewing IT security policies iv. conducting cybersecurity awareness drills
questions.question: Per CERT-In's Guidelines for Government Entities, why must the CISO's dedicated cybersecurity team be kept separate from the IT operations and infrastructure team?
options: So that security monitoring, incident response, and policy enforcement are handled independently rather than by the same team that runs day-to-day IT operations
Because IT operations staff are not permitted to use email
Because cybersecurity teams are not allowed to interact with CERT-In
Because separation eliminates the need for any cybersecurity awareness training
questions.explanation: Keeping the security function organizationally distinct from operations supports independent monitoring, incident response, and policy oversight. The other options are unrelated or contradicted by the text (the team still runs awareness drills and liaises with CERT-In).

questions.locator: Cyber Hygiene for Cyber Space (Basic), Section 2 Password Security Management, Dos
questions.source_excerpt: Strong passwords should contain combination of upper case, lower case, numbers, 'Special' characters...Always use different passwords for different accounts.
questions.question: Per I4C's Cyber Hygiene (Basic) manual's 'Dos' for password security, what should a strong password combine?
options: Upper case, lower case, numbers, and special characters
Only the user's date of birth and name
The same single word reused for every account
Only lower-case letters, kept as short as possible
questions.explanation: The manual explicitly lists this character-type combination as a strong-password requirement. The other options describe weak, guessable, or reused password practices the manual actually warns against.

questions.locator: Cyber Hygiene for Cyber Space (Basic), Section 2 Password Security Management, Don'ts
questions.source_excerpt: Do not use public systems to access banking/sensitive sites. Do not share password, OTP through e-mail, chat or any other electronic communication.
questions.question: Per I4C's Cyber Hygiene manual's 'Don'ts' for password security, what should never be shared over email or chat?
questions.explanation: The manual specifically names password and OTP as things never to share electronically. A holiday schedule, landline number, and agenda topics are not the sensitive credentials this guidance targets.

questions.locator: Cyber Hygiene for Cyber Space (Basic), Section 5 Social Media Platforms - Safety tips, Don'ts
questions.source_excerpt: Do not use social media account without Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA). Never log into social media accounts from untrusted systems.
questions.question: An officer wants to better protect their official social media account per I4C's Cyber Hygiene guidance. Which control does the manual recommend enabling?
options: Logging in only from public cyber cafes
questions.explanation: The manual recommends MFA for social media accounts. Auto-accepting requests, disabling privacy settings, and using public cyber cafes are all practices the manual actually discourages.

questions.locator: Cyber Hygiene for Cyber Space (Basic), Section 1.1 USB device Security, Dos
questions.source_excerpt: Scan USB device with Anti-virus/Endpoint Protection before its use. Autorun/Autoplay feature shall be disabled in all the computers, while using USB.
questions.question: Per I4C's Cyber Hygiene manual, what two precautions are recommended before and while using a USB drive on an office computer?
options: Scan it with anti-virus/endpoint protection first, and keep Autorun/Autoplay disabled
Enable Autorun so files open automatically for convenience
Skip scanning entirely, since USB drives cannot carry malware
Only use USB drives on personal devices, and never scan them at all
questions.explanation: The manual's own two Dos are scanning before use and disabling Autorun/Autoplay. The other options directly contradict this guidance.

questions.locator: Cyber Hygiene for Cyber Space (Basic), Section 4 Financial Transactions - Safe Practices, Dos
questions.source_excerpt: Verify the name of 'Payee' or QR code before proceeding with the payment. UPI PIN is not needed while receiving payments.
questions.question: A citizen receives a message claiming they must enter their UPI PIN to 'receive' a refund payment. Applying I4C's Cyber Hygiene guidance on UPI safety, why is this very likely a scam?
options: The manual states a UPI PIN is never needed to receive a payment, only to send one, so a request for a PIN to 'receive' money contradicts how UPI actually works
UPI PINs are required for every incoming and outgoing transaction, so the request is normal
QR codes and payee names are irrelevant to UPI safety per the manual
The manual recommends sharing UPI PINs whenever a refund is promised
questions.explanation: The manual explicitly states a UPI PIN is not needed to receive payments, which exposes the scam's false premise. The other options reverse or misstate the manual's actual guidance.

questions.source_excerpt: Vision: Democratize access to public Government data through a world-class user experience.
questions.question: What is NDAP's (National Data and Analytics Platform) officially stated Vision?
options: To democratize access to public Government data through a world-class user experience
To privatize all government datasets for commercial sale
To replace all government dashboards with printed reports
To restrict data access to only central ministries
questions.explanation: This is the document's own Vision statement. The other options describe the opposite of democratized, user-friendly public access.

questions.source_excerpt: Mission: Standardize data across multiple Government sources, provide flexible analytics and make it easily accessible in formats conducive for research, innovation, policy making and public consumption.
questions.question: Per the NDAP Vision Document, what is the platform's stated Mission built around?
options: Standardizing data across government sources and making it accessible in formats useful for research, innovation, and policymaking
Digitizing paper records only, with no analytics component
Building a single mobile app for citizen grievance redressal
Training government employees exclusively in spreadsheet software
questions.explanation: The Mission statement names standardization, flexible analytics, and accessible formats. Grievance redressal apps and spreadsheet training are not part of this stated mission.

questions.source_excerpt: User-centric -- Data access is user-friendly and engaging, tailored to the needs of policymakers, bureaucrats, researchers, innovators, data scientists, journalists and citizens alike
questions.question: NDAP lists 'User-centric' as one of its three core objectives. What does this objective specifically target?
options: Making data access friendly and engaging, tailored to the varied needs of policymakers, researchers, journalists, and citizens
Making the platform accessible only to trained IT engineers
Making all data available exclusively in PDF format
Limiting access to a single ministry's data at a time
questions.explanation: The document explicitly names this broad set of user groups the objective is tailored to. Restricting access to IT staff, one format, or one ministry contradicts the stated aim.

questions.source_excerpt: Coherent -- Multiple data sets are presented using a standardized schema, by using common geographical and temporal identifiers
questions.question: NDAP's 'Coherent' objective is achieved by presenting datasets using a standardized schema with common identifiers for which two dimensions?
options: Geographical and temporal (region and time period) identifiers
Employee ID and department code identifiers only
questions.explanation: The Coherent objective specifically names common geographical and temporal identifiers as the standardizing mechanism. The other pairs are not what the document describes.

questions.source_excerpt: Up-to-date -- Standard Operating Procedures are set to ensure data is updated regularly
questions.question: How does the NDAP Vision Document propose to keep data 'Up-to-date' as one of its core objectives?
options: By establishing Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) that ensure data is updated regularly
By updating data only once every ten years
By deleting older datasets instead of updating them
By relying solely on citizens to manually correct government data
questions.explanation: The document names SOPs for regular updates as the mechanism. Infrequent updates, deletion, or relying solely on citizen correction are not what it describes.

questions.source_excerpt: Websites of over 50 Ministries and Departments of the Central Government and data.gov.in. Websites of all Departments and Ministries of the State Government, not exceeding 250
questions.question: Per the NDAP Vision Document's 'Data Sources' section, roughly how many Central Government Ministries and Departments (plus data.gov.in) were named as sources?
questions.explanation: The document states 'over 50 Ministries and Departments' as a Central Government data source, alongside data.gov.in. The other figures do not match the stated source count.

questions.source_excerpt: Data is not published in a user-centric manner. The current data formats are often not conducive for research and innovation...some datasets are only available in PDF, webpage or as an image, making it difficult for further analysis.
questions.question: Per the NDAP Vision Document's 'Challenges' section, why are datasets published only as PDF, webpage, or image formats considered a problem for data literacy and analysis?
options: Such formats are difficult to extract data from and analyze programmatically, costing researchers significant time compared to machine-readable formats
PDF and image files cannot be viewed on any government computer
Webpages and PDFs are illegal formats for a government to publish data in
Such formats always contain incorrect data compared to spreadsheets
questions.explanation: The document's own reasoning is that these formats are hard to clean and prepare for analysis, wasting researcher time -- not that they are unviewable, illegal, or inherently inaccurate.

questions.locator: NDAP Vision Document, Challenges -- incoherent data ecosystem
questions.source_excerpt: Data ecosystem is incoherent due to different standards. Ministries and Departments do not use a shared standard for common indicators. Attributes like region and time period defined differently...a District Magistrate can access data across all departments for their district, easily, in one platform.
questions.question: The NDAP Vision Document uses the example of a District Magistrate wanting cross-department data for their district to illustrate the benefit of solving which challenge?
options: The lack of a shared data standard (coherence) across different ministries and departments
The lack of internet connectivity in district offices
The shortage of trained data-entry staff
The absence of printed government reports
questions.explanation: The District Magistrate example directly follows the discussion of incoherent, differently-defined standards across departments, illustrating the payoff of solving that specific coherence problem.

questions.source_excerpt: We intend to draw inspiration from the best platforms around the world...platforms such as 'datausa.io' and 'data.gov.sg'.
questions.question: Per the NDAP Vision Document's 'Approach' section, which two international platforms are named as sources of inspiration?
questions.explanation: The document names exactly these two platforms as inspiration for NDAP's user experience. The other pairs are not mentioned in this section.

questions.locator: NDAP Vision Document, Approach -- building on Indian platforms
questions.source_excerpt: data.gov.in provides ready access to data from 165 departments.
questions.question: Per the NDAP Vision Document, roughly how many departments' data does the existing Indian platform data.gov.in provide ready access to?
questions.explanation: The document states data.gov.in provides access to 165 departments' data. The other figures do not match this stated number.

questions.source_excerpt: DISHA, by the Ministry of Rural Development, provides access to data from 42 schemes across 20 ministries.
questions.question: Per the NDAP Vision Document, the DISHA platform (Ministry of Rural Development) provides access to data covering how many schemes and ministries?
questions.explanation: The document states this specific figure for DISHA. The other counts do not match the text.

questions.source_excerpt: Data export in machine readable format -- Facilitate analysis in R, Tableau, SAS...Enable cross sectoral Analysis
questions.question: A researcher wants to import NDAP data directly into a statistical tool like R for analysis, without manually re-typing values. Which NDAP feature makes this possible?
questions.explanation: The document names machine-readable export (facilitating R/Tableau/SAS analysis) as the relevant feature. The other items are unrelated to importing data into an analysis tool.

questions.locator: NDAP Vision Document, Features -- Common schema
questions.source_excerpt: Common schema across sectors -- ...Enable easy access to data from different sectors
questions.question: What is the purpose of NDAP presenting data using a 'common schema across sectors,' per the Vision Document's Features section?
options: To let users easily access and compare data drawn from different sectors, such as health, education, and finance, within one consistent structure
To ensure only one sector's data is ever visible on the platform at a time
To require every dataset to be converted into a PDF before publishing
To restrict cross-sector access to only NITI Aayog staff
questions.explanation: The document links a common schema to easy access across sectors. The other options describe restrictions the feature is not meant to create.

questions.locator: NDAP Vision Document, Features -- Database of innovation
questions.source_excerpt: Database of innovation with public data -- Showcase innovative uses and top research articles for every search result
questions.question: Which NDAP feature is meant to highlight innovative uses and top research articles connected to a user's search on the platform?
options: Database of innovation with public data
questions.explanation: This is the feature's own stated purpose in the document. The other options are unrelated governance or unrelated-document artifacts.

questions.locator: NDAP Vision Document, Governance Structure -- High Powered Steering Committee
questions.source_excerpt: A high powered inter-ministerial steering committee under the chairmanship of Vice Chairman, NITI Aayog will be set up to provide direction, oversee progress, guide on data sources, and address various inter-ministerial issues
questions.question: Per the NDAP Vision Document's Governance Structure, who chairs the High Powered Steering Committee overseeing the platform?
options: The CEO of a private technology vendor
questions.explanation: The document names the Vice Chairman, NITI Aayog as chair of this committee. The other roles are not stated as chairing it.

questions.locator: NDAP Vision Document, Governance Structure -- Technical Advisory Group
questions.source_excerpt: Technical Advisory Group consisting of sector and technology experts will be established to provide expert consultation. TAG will provide guidance on the development of the platform, management of data, and aligning the platform for user-needs.
questions.question: What role does the Technical Advisory Group (TAG) play in NDAP's governance structure, per the Vision Document?
options: Providing expert consultation and guidance on platform development, data management, and aligning it to user needs
Directly writing all of the application's code
Approving the annual government budget for all ministries
Replacing the High Powered Steering Committee entirely
questions.explanation: The document describes TAG's role as expert consultation and guidance, not budget approval, coding, or replacing the steering committee.

questions.locator: NDAP Vision Document, Governance Structure -- Project Management Unit
questions.source_excerpt: Project Management Unit -- Established at NITI Aayog to coordinate with different stakeholders and manage various facets of NDAP
questions.question: Per the NDAP Vision Document, where is the Project Management Unit that coordinates NDAP's stakeholders established?
options: At the Reserve Bank of India
questions.explanation: The document states the Project Management Unit is established at NITI Aayog. The other locations are not mentioned in this role.

questions.source_excerpt: The first version of National Data and Analytics Platform is proposed to be released in 2021. NDAP is a pan-India initiative...Its success requires extensive support and cooperation of various stakeholders such as Central Ministries, State Governments and guidance from experts
questions.question: Why does the NDAP Vision Document describe the platform's success as dependent on 'extensive support and cooperation' from Central Ministries, State Governments, and experts, rather than something NITI Aayog can deliver alone?
options: Because NDAP's value depends on aggregating and standardizing data that originates from many different ministries and state governments, whose underlying data collection NITI Aayog does not directly control
Because NITI Aayog lacks the legal authority to create any government platform
Because the platform is entirely built and hosted by state governments with no central role at all
Because cooperation is only needed for choosing the platform's name
questions.explanation: NDAP is fundamentally an aggregation of data that ministries and states themselves collect and own, so their cooperation is structurally necessary -- the other options either invent a legal barrier or trivialize the described dependency.
